title: Chat-Based Coding — Describe What You Want, Get Code Back

panels.prompt: A dramatic product launch moment: a glowing screen showing the ChatGPT logo with the date 'November 30, 2022' below it, a massive wave of tiny user icons flooding toward the screen from all directions, a counter reaching '100 Million Users' in bright text, sense of explosive viral growth, energetic and exciting atmosphere, dark background. Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, violet and golden accent lighting

panels.text: On November 30, 2022, OpenAI launched ChatGPT. It reached 100 million monthly active users by January 2023 — the fastest-growing consumer application in history. Developers discovered it was shockingly good at writing code from plain English descriptions.

When GPT-4 arrived on March 14, 2023, the leap in code quality was dramatic. Claude, from Anthropic — co-founded by Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei with a safety-first approach — entered the space in March 2023, followed by Claude 2 in July with a 100,000-token context window.

panels.prompt: A developer hunched over their desk, exhausted, surrounded by a visual circular loop: a chat window with code -> an arrow to a terminal where code is pasted -> the terminal showing a red ERROR -> an arrow back to the chat window -> new code generated -> arrow back to the terminal. The arrows form a giant hamster wheel shape around the developer. The developer looks tired and frustrated. Labels on each station: 'Chat', 'Copy', 'Paste', 'Run', 'Error', 'Copy Error', 'Chat Again'. On the right, an arrow breaks OUT of the circle, glowing violet, labeled 'What if AI could do steps 3-6 ITSELF?' Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes

panels.text: The AI could write code — but it could not run code. It could not see your project. Every interaction followed the same exhausting loop: describe, get code, copy, paste, run, hit error, copy error, go back, get fix, copy again… The human was the bottleneck.

panels.caption: The Copy-Paste Hamster Wheel — humans as the bottleneck between AI and the computer

panels.text: Chat-based coding was a revolution in capability but not in workflow. The AI got smarter, but the human still did all the running, testing, copying, and pasting. The bottleneck was not intelligence. It was the gap between the AI’s brain and the computer it needed to control.
What broke the cycle was not a smarter model. It was giving the model something it never had before: hands.
